messages.subject: Bug in anova() ?
parts:
(Unfortunately my last thread was deleted - if that had a reason, please let me know! Maybe it was my fault! ;)


Hi!

I use lavaan for testing measurement invariance. I do have an issue with reconstructing the Chi^2 difference test for nested models as proposed here: http://www.statmodel.com/chidiff.shtml
If I use the measurementInvariance() I can easily reconstruct the delta Chi^2 by using the formulas as stated on the Mplus page. When I use the anova() function for testing two nested MGCFA models (the only difference is "group.equal=c("loadings")") it seems that 
1. anova() uses the unscaled chi^2 values - which is, as far as I know, wrong. (The output even states "Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = satorra.bentler)"...)
2. Even if I use the unscaled chi^2 values, I can´t recalculated the delta-chi^2 with the known formula...

What am I doing wrong? 

PS: I can´t rely on measurementInvariance() since I am using cfa.mi() for multiple imputations from the semTools package. But that should´nt matter.

Many thanks in advance, best regards from Berlin, 

Tobias

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Bug in anova() ?
parts:
Ah but using multiple imputations should matter! The issue with any sort of nested model test using imputed data is that we simply don't know what best practice is for testing differences. This is illustrated by the issue of assessing fit with multiply imputed data. With MI you can compute 3-4 different chi square statistics. Which of these performs best remains an open question for research. So which chi square to use for model difference testing also remains an open question. For that reason we haven't built an anova method for results that come from imputed data. In your case, I'd advice using FIML with auxiliary variables to test for measurement invariance.

Hope this helps,

Alex

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Bug in anova() ?
parts: Nope you didn't do anything wrong. By default cfa.mi will display a chi square statistic similar to the one computed by Mplus (which is almost identical to the MR chi square that is also available). The documentation for runMI (or cfa.mi) contains more information about the chi square pooling options. We provide several options in runMI but there currently isn't great guidance on which to use with nested model tests (or even without). We're working on some of these issues but they remain open. Honestly we probably need better documentation on the different chi square pooling options available.

Okay. I got it now, found additional information at the Muthens' board: http://www.statmodel.com/discussion/messages/22/7831.html?1376586945
This produced a couple more questions for me: 

For validation of my 4-factorial survey I used MLM and Multiple Imputations to deal with missings. I get a fairly good model fit in a single group-CFA . I have  a small number of participants, n=135 (109 complete, 26 with missings < 5% per Item). 
I can´t test for measurement invariance with imputed datasets relying on Chi^2-Difftest , because there is no approach to do this (more exact: I can´t test nested models). 
Therefore, I have the following questions: 

Q1: Muthen (see link above) mentions Wald-Test, which is not based on log-Likelihood. Is that possible with lavaan when using MLM and imputed data in nested models?

When I just can´t test for invariance with imputed data:  The workaround would be to use MLR and FIML, but this degrades my overall model fit (I think this is because a small sample-size in MGFFA and big model, not because of model misspecification, I think there are some references on sample-size issues and MLR
)
Q2: Would it be a reasonable work-around to test for measurement invariance by using MLR and FIML for each construct separately? E.g. doing four model invariance tests?

Q3: When I proceed as mentioned in Question 2: After I have shown that there is invariance, is it reasonable, to use MLM and Multiple Imputations to constrain factor loadings an intercepts to get mean estimates on latent factors?

Thank you!
